video_title: Thrive Capital’s Dr. Nworah Ayogu on Why Neuralink Is More Interesting Than SpaceX
gist: Thrive Capital healthcare partner Dr. Nworah Ayogu argues that if you are AGI-pilled you should be long healthcare: AI drug discovery (Isomorphic) will shift bottlenecks to trials and manufacturing, hardware-bio companies (Neuralink, Forell) unlock new treatments, and clinical AI (OpenEvidence, Cadence, ChatGPT) is spreading at unprecedented speed. He frames the US system's $40T decade with flat life expectancy as the core opportunity and predicts more trillion-dollar healthcare companies plus aggressive incumbent build-or-buy.

themes.theme: AI drug discovery stack and bottleneck shifts

insights.claim: AI's impact on biotech will flow through the entire value chain (manufacturing, clinical development, commercialization), analogous to how AI lab demand flowed through compute, memory and energy supply chains.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Look for second-order biotech picks-and-shovels plays beyond discovery models (CDMOs, trial infrastructure, commercialization).
insights.quote: We're going to see the same thing with, you know, biotech where it's not just drug discovery, it's going to be manufacturing

insights.claim: AI drug discovery progresses through three prediction problems: designing a molecule that binds the target, predicting on-target biological effects, and predicting off-target side effects; binding prediction is largely improving while effect prediction is the next frontier.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Value in AI biotech is migrating from structure/binding models toward biology/effect prediction and the data that trains it.
insights.quote: the first step of what molecule binds well is the thing we've actually gotten, you know, better and better and better at doing

insights.claim: Unlike code or math, biology outputs are not cheaply verifiable; confirming effects requires cell, animal and human testing, so proprietary data generation for training effect-prediction models is a key bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Companies generating proprietary wet-lab/clinical data for model training hold a structural moat.
insights.quote: with coding, with math, you know, those things are very verifiable. So I can I know whether my code compiles or not

insights.claim: Isomorphic Labs' stated aspiration (per Max at the Biohub event) is to move drug development from 90%+ failure rates toward ~88-90% success rates, and from a 10-15 year process toward roughly four years.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: If even partially realized, pipeline economics and pharma R&D ROI would be re-rated dramatically.
insights.quote: he said for like 88 to 90% success rates for a process right now that has 90 plus% failure rates. takes 10 to 15 years and costs billions of dollars

insights.claim: Raising clinical success from ~5% to ~60% would radically change which programs drug developers are willing to pursue across the whole process.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Higher probability of success expands the set of economically viable targets and indications.
insights.quote: Rather than having a 5% success rate, I can have a 60% success rate. Like that's that's amazing because that radically changes the things I'm willing

insights.claim: As preclinical discovery accelerates, clinical trials (Phase 1-3) and then manufacturing become the bottlenecks; ARPA and government agencies are working on clinical-trial efficiency.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Trial-acceleration and agile manufacturing are the next investable chokepoints if new drugs arrive every ~3 years rather than 10.
insights.quote: what we don't want to do is get very good at sort of pre-clinical and still have the clinical be the bottleneck

insights.claim: Ayogu rebuts critics who see Isomorphic as only a protein-folding shop, arguing the team invented the field with AlphaFold (Nobel to Demis Hassabis) and has long worked on downstream steps.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Thrive's thesis is that Isomorphic is a full-stack drug developer, not a single-model company.
insights.quote: ISO and team invented protein folding with alpha fold right that is that is why Demis got the Nobel Prize

insights.claim: Thrive's core selection filter is 'bilingual' companies that are world-class at both AI/technology and the domain science; Isomorphic's chemists and biologists are said to match Lilly, Pfizer, Broad and Whitehead caliber while its AI researchers match DeepMind, Anthropic and OpenAI.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Useful diligence lens: dual-excellence teams over AI-wrapper or pure-bio teams.
insights.quote: we want companies that are bilingual. So, we want companies that are, you know, truly the best at both of what they do

insights.claim: Thrive got into Isomorphic Labs although Demis Hassabis was not raising, via Josh Kushner's relationship-building and conviction that healthcare is where much of AI's benefit will land.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Thrive wins allocation in non-raising AI leaders through founder relationships and domain fluency.

insights.claim: One biotech CEO told OpenAI leadership roughly two years ago that AI would never be useful for drug discovery beyond customer service, and has since announced billions of dollars of AI spend.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Incumbent pharma belief in AI flipped fast; enterprise AI spend in pharma is now large.
insights.quote: I don't really think though these tools will ever be useful in drug discovery." And now I'm seeing two years later

themes.theme: Why healthcare is the AGI trade

insights.claim: If you are 'AGI-pilled' you should be long healthcare, because as AI abundance grows people will direct personal and societal spend toward more time and better quality time, i.e. healthcare (and entertainment).
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Frames healthcare as the primary beneficiary of AI-driven abundance, implying more trillion-dollar healthcare companies.
insights.quote: if you're truly AGI pill as they say right you should be actually long healthare

insights.claim: Merck's Keytruda generated more 2025 revenue as a single drug than all the major AI labs combined, showing biotech is already big business.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Single-asset biotech revenue scale rivals frontier AI; supports valuation upside in biotech platforms.
insights.quote: Kuda's 2025 revenue of just that one drug was larger than the revenue of all the major labs combined

insights.claim: Merck and Moderna's personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine, combined with Keytruda, reduced five-year recurrence by about 50% in Phase 3, per Ayogu, and checkpoint inhibitors keep finding new combination uses.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Combination use extends checkpoint-inhibitor franchises and validates individualized mRNA oncology.
insights.quote: people who had that were 50% less likely to have a recurrence of that cancer in five years

insights.claim: Eli Lilly beat first-mover Novo Nordisk in GLP-1s largely by investing in manufacturing to relieve shortages about a year before Novo and by innovating commercially with LillyDirect, not just on science.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: In biotech, supply-chain and commercial innovation can trump first-mover science advantage.
insights.quote: Lily got there a year beforehand so they had more supply out there

insights.claim: Because AI makes building easier, new biotech companies are starting with more surface area (science plus manufacturing plus care delivery), making them more defensible and expanding TAM, which is why more trillion-dollar healthcare companies will emerge.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Favor vertically ambitious biotech/healthcare startups over narrow single-layer players.
insights.quote: it makes their businesses more defensible but also gives them a much bigger TAM

insights.claim: US healthcare spending is about $5 trillion a year and projected to reach $9 trillion by the end of the decade.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Enormous and growing spend pool for AI-driven cost and productivity plays.
insights.quote: we spend 5 trillion a year now right and that's projected actually to go to 9 trillion by the end of the decade

insights.claim: Healthcare is the largest US employer (about 20% of jobs), is projected to account for about 30% of new jobs, and is the largest federal budget line item at six times defense.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Labor productivity in healthcare is a bigger macro lever than defense, which is drawing outsized VC attention.
insights.quote: It's the largest line item in the federal budget, six times the size of defense.

insights.claim: Over the last decade the US spent roughly $40 trillion on healthcare without moving life expectancy (about 80 years), which Ayogu calls an indictment of the system; cancer mortality gains were offset by overdoses and similar factors.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Outcome-based models that move hard endpoints are where value and political tailwinds lie.
insights.quote: for the last 10 years we've spent about 40 trillion on healthcare we have not moved our life expectancy an inch

insights.claim: Historic US life expectancy gains came in two waves: 50 to 70 (1900-1950) from sanitation, child mortality, antibiotics and vaccines, and 70 to 80 (1990-2010) from cardiovascular gains split roughly half smoking reduction and half statins and blood-pressure control.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Signals that the next leap needs a new class of science-driven interventions.

insights.claim: Ayogu argues that if the system does its job, the next ten years should take US life expectancy from 80 to 100.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Extremely bullish longevity framing that underpins Thrive's healthcare conviction.
insights.quote: this next 10-year period is a period where we went from 80 to 100

insights.claim: Inequality in outcomes is large: Hawaii averages about 80 years vs West Virginia about 72, and the richest vs poorest 1% of men differ by about 15 years.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Access-equalizing models (virtual care, AI) target a large outcome gap.

insights.claim: N-of-1 medicine is real: Penn designed and delivered a custom gene-editing therapy to baby KJ within about six months, costing about $1.5 million, and the bottleneck shifts to scalable, cheaper manufacturing and payment models.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Infrastructure to make bespoke therapies repeatable and cheaper is a key investable gap.
insights.quote: it took a million and a half dollars to actually make the treatment and deliver it

themes.theme: Neuralink, Forell and the hardware-bio intersection

insights.claim: Ayogu's hot take is that Neuralink is a more interesting company than SpaceX because the brain is vaster than space and remains a more efficient compute engine than any Nvidia chip.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Positions BCI as a frontier category with potentially SpaceX-scale ambition.
insights.quote: I think Neurolink is a more interesting company than SpaceX. The brain is vaster than space.

insights.claim: Neuralink vertically integrates mission-critical functions, including a custom surgical robot to implant 1,000+ microscopic threads and an in-house pathology lab, which Ayogu had never seen a company insource.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Elon-style vertical integration creates capabilities that would each be standalone companies elsewhere.
insights.quote: I've never met a company before that insourced their own pathology lab

insights.claim: Neuralink compounded its lead by creating the BCI category; talent density and category leadership attract top hardware engineers (SpaceX/Tesla/Optimus level), neurosurgeons and pathologists.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Category creators retain talent moats that compound over time.
insights.quote: they didn't just step out into the lead, they created the category

insights.claim: Hearing loss affects 1.5 billion people and is the greatest modifiable risk factor for dementia, raising dementia likelihood by about one-third.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Hearing tech is a dementia-prevention market, not just a consumer device.
insights.quote: folks who have hearing loss also have a one-third increase in their likelihood to have dementia

insights.claim: Conventional hearing aids amplify all sound; Forell uses custom-taped-out chips (via TSMC) and semantic noise processing to selectively amplify, addressing size, all-day battery and fast inference constraints.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Custom silicon plus AI audio is the differentiator against incumbent amplification devices.
insights.quote: Most hearing aids just increase everything.

insights.claim: Forell scored a 6 on an independent third-party hearing-aid rating scale where the previous highest score ever was 4.5 out of 5, and has a waitlist with users including Steve Martin and Henry Kravis.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Strong product-market signal ahead of supply ramp; capacity is the near-term constraint.
insights.quote: 4.5 was their highest rating that a hearing aid had ever gotten on their fivepoint scale forel recently did it and got a six

insights.claim: Ayogu segments healthcare AI adoption into back office (revenue cycle management, fastest because it makes money), front office (voice agents for scheduling and outreach) and in-office (scribes, then OpenEvidence).
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Adoption sequencing follows direct revenue impact first, then labor, then clinical decision support.
insights.quote: there's front office there's back office and there's in office is kind of the division I like to use for healthcare

insights.claim: OpenEvidence reached about two-thirds of US physicians in three years, while Epic has less than 50% of physicians after 40 years.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Shows unprecedented adoption speed in a notoriously hard user base; clinician-loved tools can beat incumbents.
insights.quote: Epic has less than 50% of physicians using their product after 40 years. Open evidence after three years got to 2/3.

insights.claim: Doctors don't dislike technology, they dislike bad enterprise health IT forced on them; voluntary enthusiasm for a clinical tool is a rare, strong signal.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Organic clinician word-of-mouth is a leading indicator for health IT winners.
insights.quote: they just don't like the bad technology that they're forced to use all the time

insights.claim: Before o1's release, Ayogu found OpenAI's reasoning model solved NEJM case challenges 10 out of 10 weeks, versus perhaps 2 in 10 for top doctors, and health system CEOs initially treated the claim as heresy.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: AI diagnostic capability arrived ahead of incumbent belief, creating a lag to exploit.
insights.quote: the 01 was batten a 10 out of 10

insights.claim: OpenAI is arguably one of the largest healthcare providers, with about 300 million people asking ChatGPT healthcare questions weekly; healthcare is the hero use case for most people the way coding is for Silicon Valley.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Consumer AI is becoming the front door of healthcare, shifting where system bottlenecks and resources go.
insights.quote: for Silicon Valley it's coding for the rest of America it is healthcare

insights.claim: OpenAI partnered with Boston Children's and Harvard hospitals on about 300 unsolved pediatric cases and reached new diagnoses for about 20.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Evidence of AI value in rare/undiagnosed disease.

insights.claim: If AI handles more self-triage, specialists could focus on cases needing them; e.g. orthopedic waits in LA of three to four months could fall to about one month since surgeons spend about half their time on non-operative cases.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Second-order effect: AI reallocates scarce specialist supply rather than replacing it.
insights.quote: there's a three month four month wait for an orthopedic surgeon in LA

insights.claim: Ayogu argues the US needs a '10x nurse' more than a '10x engineer', i.e. AI should amplify the healthcare workforce, not just consumers.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Clinician-productivity tooling is a large underweighted opportunity.
insights.quote: as a nation, I think we need a 10x nurse a lot more than we need a 10x engineer

insights.claim: Cadence, a remote patient monitoring company built with health systems, operates in about 7,000 sites of care with over 100,000 patients, reporting 25% fewer hospitalizations, 80%+ more patients with controlled blood pressure, nearly a full point A1C reduction, and $2.5M of Medicare savings per week.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Hard-outcome, cost-saving RPM is a model for value-based AI care.
insights.quote: They save Medicare $2.5 million every week.

insights.claim: Cadence's AI med-titration agents learn each prescriber's patterns and reach 98% concordance with doctors, and contacting patients at the moment of measurement raised reach rates by 70%.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Human-AI integration, not replacement, drives clinical results and efficiency.
insights.quote: they've had a 70% increase in the amount and getting a hold of folks with AI

themes.theme: Incumbents, M&A and Thrive portfolio outcomes

insights.claim: Incumbents will not be flat-footed in AI healthcare: they will build or buy, as with Lilly launching a lab with Nvidia, Oracle moving fast, and McKesson buying large oncology care providers, while some startups IPO as standalones.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Expect both active healthcare AI M&A and standalone IPOs; exits are not limited to one path.
insights.quote: incumbents aren't flatfooted in the age of AI and they're going to either try to build or buy the capabilities they need

insights.claim: Value-chain players are moving into adjacent lanes, e.g. distributor McKesson buying care delivery assets and biotechs expanding into care delivery, because it is easier to build.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Watch for cross-layer vertical integration reshaping healthcare competitive maps.
insights.quote: McKessen has gone out and bought large oncology providers

insights.claim: Oscar Health fell about 95% from peak in December 2022 but is back above its IPO price, up about 100% year-over-year, defying a hard period for health insurers thanks to its decade-old tech-first claims stack enabling fast AI adoption.
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Modern infrastructure built early is a compounding advantage in the AI era for insurers.
insights.quote: now it's back up above its IPO price I think it's uh increased 100% year-over-year

insights.claim: Amazon's healthcare entry sequenced from its logistics advantage (PillPack into Amazon Pharmacy) to low-acuity transactional care (Amazon Clinic) to low-acuity relational care (One Medical acquisition).
insights.speaker: Nworah Ayogu (Thrive Capital)
insights.so_what: Big-tech healthcare expansion follows trust ladders from transactional to relational.
